I’d merge these **ten, in this order**, starting with the most contained changes. All target `main`, so there are no stacked-parent dependencies to manage.

| Order | Trail | Why I recommend it |

| 7 | [#220](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/220) | Fixes multi-pattern Git grep hangs and subprocess cleanup on cancellation. |
| 8 | [#234](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/234) | Reduces cache-writing memory use and avoids decoding an entire cache just to verify it. |
| 9 | [#231](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/231) | Removes repeated copying during same-name candidate lookup. |
| 10 | [#232](https://entire.io/gh/entireio/entire-graph/trails/232) | Reads bounded annotation windows without splitting whole files. |

I verified **31 green CI checks, all seven runners passed on the current head, and zero open findings for every selected trail**. Each also merges cleanly with current main.

These are recommendations, not all equally low risk: the cancellation and core performance changes deserve more scrutiny. All ten branches are **38 commits behind main**, so synchronize and refresh checks as you land them.
